theorem ccmGuinandWeilCompletedSourceWindow_eq_xiScrewGreen
    {b H : ℝ} (hb0 : 0 < b) (hbH : b ≤ H)
    {F F' F'' : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hF : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc b H, HasDerivAt F (F' x) x)
    (hF' : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc b H, HasDerivAt F' (F'' x) x)
    (hF''cont : ContinuousOn F'' (Set.Icc b H)) :
    ccmGuinandWeilCompletedSourceWindow b H F =
      -F H * (ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewRightSlope H -
          ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewRightSlope b) +
        F' H * ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal b H -
          ∫ h in b..H,
            ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal b h * F'' h

theorem ccmGuinandWeilCompletedSourceWindow_eq_xiScrewGreen
    {b H : ℝ} (hb0 : 0 < b) (hbH : b ≤ H)
    {F F' F'' : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hF : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc b H, HasDerivAt F (F' x) x)
    (hF' : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc b H, HasDerivAt F' (F'' x) x)
    (hF''cont : ContinuousOn F'' (Set.Icc b H)) :
    ccmGuinandWeilCompletedSourceWindow b H F =
      -F H * (ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewRightSlope H -
          ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewRightSlope b) +
        F' H * ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal b H -
          ∫ h in b..H,
            ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal b h * F'' h
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hcontinuous :
      (∫ h in b..H,
        F h * (ccmPublishedArchimedeanDensity h - 2 * Real.cosh (h / 2))) =
        -(∫ h in b..H, F h * screwRegularKernel h) := by
    rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_neg]
    apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
    intro h hh
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hbH] at hh
    change F h * (ccmPublishedArchimedeanDensity h -
      2 * Real.cosh (h / 2)) = -(F h * screwRegularKernel h)
    rw [ccmPublishedArchimedeanDensity_sub_two_cosh_eq_neg_screwRegularKernel
      (hb0.trans_le hh.1)]
    ring
  have hprime := ccmGuinandWeilPrimeHingeGreenIdentity
    hb0 hbH hF hF' hF''cont
  have hsmooth := ccmGuinandWeil_smoothScrewGreenIdentity
    hb0 hbH hF hF' hF''cont
  let C : ℝ → ℝ := ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothCodiagonal b
  let P : ℝ → ℝ := ccmGuinandWeilPrimeHingeCodiagonal b H
  have hCcont : ContinuousOn C (Set.Icc b H) := by
    intro h hh
    exact ((hasDerivAt_ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothCodiagonal
      (hb0.trans_le hh.1)).continuousAt).continuousWithinAt
  have hPcont : Continuous P := by
    dsimp only [P]
    unfold ccmGuinandWeilPrimeHingeCodiagonal
    refine continuous_finsetSum _ fun k _hk => ?_
    by_cases hbk : b < Real.log k
    · simp only [hbk, if_true]
      fun_prop
    · simp only [hbk, if_false]
      fun_prop
  have hCI : IntervalIntegrable (fun h => C h * F'' h) volume b H := by
    apply ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hbH]
    exact hCcont.mul hF''cont
  have hPI : IntervalIntegrable (fun h => P h * F'' h) volume b H := by
    apply ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hbH]
    exact hPcont.continuousOn.mul hF''cont
  have hbulk :
      (∫ h in b..H, ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal b h * F'' h) =
        (∫ h in b..H, C h * F'' h) -
          ∫ h in b..H, P h * F'' h := by
    rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_sub hCI hPI]
    apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
    intro h hh
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hbH] at hh
    change ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal b h * F'' h =
      C h * F'' h - P h * F'' h
    rw [ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal_eq_smooth_sub_primeHinge
      hb0 hbH hh]
    dsimp only [C, P]
    ring
  have hcodH := ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal_eq_smooth_sub_primeHinge
    hb0 hbH (⟨hbH, le_rfl⟩ : H ∈ Set.Icc b H)
  have hslope :=
    ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewRightSlope_sub_eq_smooth_sub_primeWindowMass hbH
  rw [ccmGuinandWeilCompletedSourceWindow, hcontinuous, hprime, hsmooth, hbulk]
  dsimp only [C, P] at hbulk ⊢
  rw [hcodH, hslope]
  ring

**Conjecture → proof:** the two moments are exactly the obstruction to solving `Dg=f` with smooth support in the same aperture. Choose `r<a` containing the support of `f` and set

`A_s(x) = exp(s*x) * integral[-r,x] exp(-s*t)*f(t) dt`,

The moment constraints make both primitives vanish outside `[-r,r]`. Since `A_s' = s*A_s + f`, the two copies of `f` cancel in `g'`, and `g''=g/4+f`. Thus `g` is smooth and compactly supported strictly inside the original aperture. This is the elementary constant-coefficient Green construction; no novelty is claimed for that construction.

**Conjecture → proof:** this inverse is unique among compactly supported smooth functions. If `Dg=0`, then `h=g'-g/2` satisfies `h'=-h/2`. Multiplication by `exp(x/2)` gives a constant, which vanishes outside the compact support. Then multiplication of `g` by `exp(-x/2)` gives a second zero constant.

At a first constrained zero, every such test is strictly positive because its compact support fits an earlier positive aperture. Yet smooth near-minimizers, pulled back through the exact inverse, give strictly positive multiplier-image Rayleigh quotients below every positive tolerance. The survivor is an exact description of how zero ground can appear through completion; no smooth null vector may be assumed.

  toFun : ℝ → ℝ
  smooth : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) toFun
  supportRadius : ℝ
  supportRadius_nonneg : 0 ≤ supportRadius
  supportRadius_lt_aperture : supportRadius < a
  support_subset : Function.support toFun ⊆ Icc (-supportRadius) supportRadius

instance (a : ℝ) : CoeFun (SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore a) fun _ => ℝ → ℝ :=
  ⟨SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore.toFun⟩

theorem SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore.continuous {a : ℝ}
    (u : SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore a) : Continuous u :=
  u.smooth.continuous

theorem SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore.hasCompactSupport {a : ℝ}
    (u : SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore a) : HasCompactSupport u :=
  HasCompactSupport.of_support_subset_isCompact isCompact_Icc u.support_subset

theorem SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore.support_subset_aperture {a : ℝ}
    (u : SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore a) : Function.support u ⊆ Ioo (-a) a := by
  intro x hx
  have hxr := u.support_subset hx
  constructor
  · linarith [hxr.1, u.supportRadius_lt_aperture]
  · linarith [hxr.2, u.supportRadius_lt_aperture]

/-- Suzuki's exact scalar coefficient in the local screw expansion. -/
def suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant : ℝ :=
  (Real.log (2 * Real.pi) - (Complex.digamma (2 : ℂ)).re) / 2

/-- Prime powers visible in the difference interval `[-2a,2a]`. -/
def suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices (a : ℝ) : Finset ℕ :=
  RHTower.suzukiVisibleWeilIndices (2 * a)

/-- Literal source-locked restricted Weil form at aperture `a`. -/
def suzukiRestrictedWeilForm (a : ℝ) (u φ : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  restrictedWeilForm a suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant
    (suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a) RHTower.suzukiWeilRemainderKernel u φ

/-- Literal source-locked distributional representative. -/
def suzukiRestrictedWeilRepresentative (a : ℝ) (u : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  restrictedWeilRepresentative a suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant
    (suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a) RHTower.suzukiWeilRemainderKernel u

/-- The source-locked form is exactly Suzuki's four published blocks. -/
theorem suzukiRestrictedWeilForm_eq_fourBlocks (a : ℝ) (u φ : ℝ → ℝ) :
    suzukiRestrictedWeilForm a u φ =
      weilFinitePartBlock a u φ +
        weilScalarBlock a suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant u φ +
        weilPrimeBlock (suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a) u φ +
        weilSmoothBlock a RHTower.suzukiWeilRemainderKernel u φ := by
  rfl

/-- The source-locked four-block form uses exactly the curvature of Suzuki's origin remainder;
the independently derived hyperbolic and screw-kernel normalizations agree pointwise. -/
theorem suzukiRestrictedWeilForm_eq_originRemainderFourBlocks
    (a : ℝ) (u φ : ℝ → ℝ) :
    suzukiRestrictedWeilForm a u φ =
      weilFinitePartBlock a u φ +
        weilScalarBlock a suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant u φ +
        weilPrimeBlock (suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a) u φ +
        weilSmoothBlock a suzukiOriginRemainderCurvature u φ := by
  rw [suzukiRestrictedWeilForm_eq_fourBlocks]
  congr 1
  unfold weilSmoothBlock
  congr 1
  apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
  intro x _
  apply congrArg (fun z : ℝ => z * φ x)
  apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
  intro y _
  dsimp only
  rw [suzukiWeilRemainderKernel_eq_originCurvature]

/-- The source-locked representative has Suzuki's exact finite-part, scalar, prime, and smooth
convolution terms, with no kernel parameter left. -/
theorem suzukiRestrictedWeilRepresentative_eq (a : ℝ) (u : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) :
    suzukiRestrictedWeilRepresentative a u x =
      -(1 / 2) * cauchyFinitePart a x u -
        (2 * suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant + 1) * u x -
        (∑ n ∈ suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a,
          primePairWeight n * (u (x + Real.log n) + u (x - Real.log n))) +
        weilSmoothRepresentative a RHTower.suzukiWeilRemainderKernel u x := by
  rfl

/-- The truncated Poisson cancellation at a general `n`:
`Σ_{j,c} e_j(−ε) E(c) Π_p s_p^{|b_p|} = ((1 + ε²)[a(n) = 0] + ε[a(n) = a(n₀)]) Π_p (1 − s_p²)`. -/
theorem sum_modeCoeff_mul_weight_general {n n₀ : ℕ} (hn₀ : IsSmoothOver P n₀) (ε : ℝ) :
    ∑ j ∈ bohrModes, ∑ c ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : P => bohrModes),
        modeCoeff ε j c * ∏ p : P, primeHalf p ^ ((vecOf P n - (j • vecOf P n₀ + c)) p).natAbs =
      ((1 + ε ^ 2) * (if vecOf P n = 0 then 1 else 0) +
        ε * (if vecOf P n = vecOf P n₀ then 1 else 0)) * ∏ p : P, (1 - primeHalf p ^ 2) := by
  classical
  have hj : ∀ j : ℤ, ∑ c ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : P => bohrModes),
      modeCoeff ε j c * ∏ p : P, primeHalf p ^ ((vecOf P n - (j • vecOf P n₀ + c)) p).natAbs =
      bohrCoeff (-ε) j * (if vecOf P n - j • vecOf P n₀ = 0 then
        ∏ p : P, (1 - primeHalf p ^ 2) else 0) := by
    intro j
    simp_rw [modeCoeff, mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum]
    congr 1
    rw [← sum_bohrVec_mul_prod_pow (fun p : P => primeHalf p) (vecOf P n - j • vecOf P n₀)]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => ?_
    congr 1
    refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun p _ => ?_
    congr 2
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply, Pi.add_apply]
    ring
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => hj j), sum_bohrModes]
  have hm1 : ¬ (vecOf P n - (-1 : ℤ) • vecOf P n₀ = 0) := by
    intro h
    apply vecOf_ne_zero hn₀
    funext p
    have h1 := congrFun h p
    have h2 := vecOf_nonneg P n p
    have h3 := vecOf_nonneg P n₀ p
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Pi.zero_apply] at h1
    simp only [Pi.zero_apply]
    linarith
  have h0 : (vecOf P n - (0 : ℤ) • vecOf P n₀ = 0) ↔ vecOf P n = 0 := by
    rw [zero_smul, sub_zero]
  have h1 : (vecOf P n - (1 : ℤ) • vecOf P n₀ = 0) ↔ vecOf P n = vecOf P n₀ := by
    rw [one_smul, sub_eq_zero]
  have b0 : bohrCoeff (-ε) 0 = 1 + ε ^ 2 := by rw [bohrCoeff, if_pos rfl, neg_sq]
  have b1 : bohrCoeff (-ε) 1 = ε := by rw [bohrCoeff, if_neg (by decide), neg_neg]
  rw [if_neg hm1, b0, b1]
  simp only [h0, h1]
  split_ifs <;> ring

    Nat.Coprime (roughPart P n) (vecDen b) := by

  refine Nat.Coprime.prod_right fun p _ => Nat.Coprime.pow_right _ ?_

/-!
# Completed Guinand–Weil third grade as Xi-screw Green curvature

This module identifies the literal Xi zero-divisor object carried by the completed
four-unit source.  On positive time, Suzuki's screw is a smooth polar--Gamma sector
minus prime hinges.  Its canonical right slope therefore records completed-error
current, while its affine codiagonal is the Green primitive of the completed source.

Two integrations by parts give the universal finite-window law

`source(F) = -F(H) ΔΨ'₊ + F'(H) C_b(H) - ∫_[b,H] C_b(h) F''(h) dh`.

For the forced inverse-cubic aperture, this becomes an exact Xi-screw Green formula.
Consequently convergence of the completed third-grade rate is equivalent, without
any analytic assumption, to convergence of that zero-divisor Green functional.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Interval
open MeasureTheory Set Finset Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

open GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

/-- Smooth part of Suzuki's positive-time Xi screw, before subtracting prime hinges. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart (h : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * Real.exp (h / 2) + 4 * Real.exp (-(h / 2)) - 8 +
    screwLinearCoeff / 2 * h + screwLerchConst - screwLerchTail h

/-- Classical slope of the smooth part of Suzuki's positive-time Xi screw. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope (h : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2 * Real.exp (h / 2) - 2 * Real.exp (-(h / 2)) +
    screwLinearCoeff / 2 - screwLerchTail₁ h

/-- Canonical right slope of the positive-time Xi screw.  The cumulative critical prime mass
includes a hinge born at the endpoint. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewRightSlope (h : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope h - criticalMellinPrimeMass h

/-- Affine-normalized codiagonal of the smooth (polar--Gamma) screw sector. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothCodiagonal (b h : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart h - ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart b -
    (h - b) * ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope b

/-- Affine-normalized source codiagonal of the Xi screw based at `b`. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewCodiagonal (b h : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  suzukiPsi h - suzukiPsi b -
    (h - b) * ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewRightSlope b

theorem ccmPublishedArchimedeanDensity_sub_two_cosh_eq_neg_screwRegularKernel
    {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) :
    ccmPublishedArchimedeanDensity h - 2 * Real.cosh (h / 2) =
      -screwRegularKernel h := by
  rw [ccmPublishedArchimedeanDensity_eq_exp_neg_half_div hh,
    screwRegularKernel_eq_tailForm hh]
  rw [Real.cosh_eq]
  ring

theorem criticalMellinAtomWeight_eq_screwPrimeWeight
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) :
    criticalMellinAtomWeight k = screwPrimeWeight k := by
  have hk0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ k := by positivity
  unfold criticalMellinAtomWeight screwPrimeWeight
  rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, show (-1 / 2 : ℝ) = -(1 / 2 : ℝ) by ring,
    Real.rpow_neg hk0, div_eq_mul_inv]
  ring

theorem suzukiPsi_eq_smoothPart_sub_screwPrimeSum
    {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h) :
    suzukiPsi h =
      ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart h - screwPrimeSum h := by
  rw [suzukiPsi, abs_of_nonneg hh]
  unfold screwFn ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart
  ring

theorem hasDerivAt_ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart
    {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) :
    HasDerivAt ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart
      (ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope h) h := by
  have htail := hasDerivAt_screwLerchTail hh
  have hpos := (hasDerivAt_exp_half h).const_mul (4 : ℝ)
  have hneg := (hasDerivAt_exp_neg_half h).const_mul (4 : ℝ)
  have hlin : HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => screwLinearCoeff / 2 * y)
      (screwLinearCoeff / 2) h := by
    simpa only [id_eq, mul_one] using
      (hasDerivAt_id h).const_mul (screwLinearCoeff / 2)
  have hraw := ((((hpos.fun_add hneg).sub_const 8).fun_add hlin).add_const
    screwLerchConst).fun_sub htail
  unfold ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope
  apply hraw.congr_deriv
  ring

theorem hasDerivAt_ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope
    {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) :
    HasDerivAt ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope
      (screwRegularKernel h) h := by
  have htail := hasDerivAt_screwLerchTail₁ hh
  have hpos := (hasDerivAt_exp_half h).const_mul (2 : ℝ)
  have hneg := (hasDerivAt_exp_neg_half h).const_mul (2 : ℝ)
  have hraw := ((hpos.fun_sub hneg).add_const
    (screwLinearCoeff / 2)).fun_sub htail
  unfold ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope
  apply hraw.congr_deriv
  rw [screwRegularKernel_eq_tailForm hh, screwLerchTail₂_eq hh]
  ring

theorem hasDerivAt_ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothCodiagonal
    {b h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) :
    HasDerivAt (ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothCodiagonal b)
      (ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope h -
        ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothSlope b) h := by
  have hsmooth := hasDerivAt_ccmGuinandWeilXiScrewSmoothPart hh
  have haff : HasDerivAt

/-!
# Exact arithmetic atoms of the moving Weil pole matrix

The frozen matrix is a smooth Gamma–polar term minus literal finite Mangoldt
atoms. Increasing the integer cutoff by one subtracts precisely the new atom.
Both atoms vanish at entry and vanish identically outside prime-power support.
-/

open Set Filter
open scoped Topology BigOperators
noncomputable section
namespace RHTower

/-- Smooth Gamma and polar part of the moving positive-pole diagonal. -/
def ccmWeilPoleDiagonalSmooth (s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2*(-Real.eulerMascheroniConstant-Real.log (2*Real.pi))*Real.sinh s-Real.exp s+
    (2*s+1)*Real.exp (-s)+8*s*Real.sinh s+ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryPrimitive s

/-- Smooth Gamma and polar part of the moving opposite-pole entry. -/
def ccmWeilPoleCrossSmooth (s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (-Real.eulerMascheroniConstant-Real.log (2*Real.pi))*(2*s)+2*s^(2 : ℕ)+
    (2*Real.sinh s)^(2 : ℕ)+ccmGammaPoleCrossBoundaryPrimitive s

/-- Literal Mangoldt diagonal atom before its subtraction from the Weil form. -/
def ccmWeilPolePrimeDiagonalAtom (n : ℕ) (s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2*ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n*(Real.exp s/n-Real.exp (-s))

/-- Literal Mangoldt cross atom before its subtraction from the Weil form. -/
def ccmWeilPolePrimeCrossAtom (n : ℕ) (s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n*(1+1/(n:ℝ))*(2*s-Real.log n)

private theorem psi_sum (X : ℝ) :
    Chebyshev.psi X = ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 ⌊X⌋₊, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n := by
  rw [Chebyshev.psi_eq_sum_Icc]
  symm
  apply Finset.sum_subset
  · intro n hn
    exact Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨Nat.zero_le _,(Finset.mem_Icc.mp hn).2⟩
  · intro n hn hnot
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc] at hn hnot
    have hsmall : n=0 ∨ n=1 := by omega
    rcases hsmall with rfl | rfl <;> simp

/-- Exact frozen diagonal as its smooth source minus every visible arithmetic atom. -/
theorem ccmWeilPoleChamberDiagonal_eq_sum_atoms (a : SuzukiPositiveAperture) (s : ℝ) :
    ccmWeilPoleChamberDiagonal a s = ccmWeilPoleDiagonalSmooth s-
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 ⌊Real.exp (2*a.1)⌋₊, ccmWeilPolePrimeDiagonalAtom n s := by
  rw [ccmWeilPoleChamberDiagonal_eq_explicit]
  have hsum : (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 ⌊Real.exp (2*a.1)⌋₊, ccmWeilPolePrimeDiagonalAtom n s) =
      2*Real.exp s*ccmReciprocalMangoldtCumulative (Real.exp (2*a.1))-
        2*Real.exp (-s)*Chebyshev.psi (Real.exp (2*a.1)) := by
    rw [ccmReciprocalMangoldtCumulative,psi_sum,Finset.mul_sum,Finset.mul_sum,
      ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro n hn
    unfold ccmWeilPolePrimeDiagonalAtom
    ring
  rw [hsum]
  unfold ccmWeilPoleDiagonalSmooth
  ring

/-- Exact frozen cross entry as its smooth source minus the affine arithmetic atoms. -/
theorem ccmWeilPoleChamberCross_eq_sum_atoms (a : SuzukiPositiveAperture) (s : ℝ) :
    ccmWeilPoleChamberCross a s = ccmWeilPoleCrossSmooth s-
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 ⌊Real.exp (2*a.1)⌋₊, ccmWeilPolePrimeCrossAtom n s := by
  rw [ccmWeilPoleChamberCross_eq_explicit]
  have hsum : ccmPolarPrimeTent a+2*(s-a.1)*ccmWeilPrimeChamberWeight a =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 ⌊Real.exp (2*a.1)⌋₊, ccmWeilPolePrimeCrossAtom n s := by
    unfold ccmPolarPrimeTent ccmWeilPrimeChamberWeight
    rw [Finset.mul_sum,← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro n hn
    unfold ccmWeilPolePrimeCrossAtom
    ring
  rw [hsum]
  rfl

/-- Both arithmetic atoms vanish identically when the integer is not a prime power. -/
theorem ccmWeilPolePrimeAtoms_zero_of_not_primePow {n : ℕ} (hn : ¬IsPrimePow n) (s : ℝ) :
    ccmWeilPolePrimeDiagonalAtom n s = 0 ∧ ccmWeilPolePrimeCrossAtom n s = 0 := by
  simp [ccmWeilPolePrimeDiagonalAtom,ccmWeilPolePrimeCrossAtom,
    ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_eq_zero_iff.mpr hn]

/-- Both actual arithmetic atoms vanish at their entry radius. -/
theorem ccmWeilPolePrimeAtoms_zero_at_entry (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ccmWeilPolePrimeDiagonalAtom n (ccmWeilIntegerEntry n hn).1 = 0 ∧
    ccmWeilPolePrimeCrossAtom n (ccmWeilIntegerEntry n hn).1 = 0 := by
  let b := ccmWeilIntegerEntry n hn
  have he : Real.exp b.1/n = Real.exp (-b.1) := by
    rw [← exp_two_mul_ccmWeilIntegerEntry n hn,← Real.exp_sub]
    congr 1
    dsimp [b]
    ring
  constructor
  · change 2*ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n*(Real.exp b.1/n-Real.exp (-b.1)) = 0
    rw [he,sub_self,mul_zero]
  · unfold ccmWeilPolePrimeCrossAtom ccmWeilIntegerEntry
    dsimp
    ring

/-- Crossing one integer cutoff subtracts exactly its diagonal prime atom. -/
theorem ccmWeilPoleChamberDiagonal_succ_cutoff (a b : SuzukiPositiveAperture)
    (hf : ⌊Real.exp (2*b.1)⌋₊ = ⌊Real.exp (2*a.1)⌋₊+1) (s : ℝ) :
    ccmWeilPoleChamberDiagonal b s-ccmWeilPoleChamberDiagonal a s =
      -ccmWeilPolePrimeDiagonalAtom (⌊Real.exp (2*a.1)⌋₊+1) s := by
  have hn : 2 ≤ ⌊Real.exp (2*a.1)⌋₊+1 := by
    have : 1 ≤ ⌊Real.exp (2*a.1)⌋₊ := Nat.le_floor (by
      simpa using Real.one_le_exp_iff.mpr (by linarith [a.2] : 0 ≤ 2*a.1))
    omega

/-!
# Positive-frequency Hardy-fiber Poisson criterion

The fixed-fiber Poisson margin is already unconditional on `|Re z| ≤ 4`.  The source trace obeys
the exact involution `z ↦ -conj z`, while ordinary conjugation of a Xi divisor point sends its
centered coordinate `α` to `-conj α`, preserves multiplicity, and transports its Poisson kernel
without loss.

Consequently one need not prove a whole-strip inequality.  For any critical Xi fiber `ρ`, RH is
equivalent to its positive-frequency Poisson margin above four.  Indeed that positive margin first
implies the ordinary positive-tail source sign; the existing source reflection and the preceding
unconditional central theorem then discharge every other frequency.  A symmetric two-channel
assembly with the Schwarz-conjugate fiber is also recorded, but is not needed for the sharp
criterion.
-/

open Complex Set

namespace RHTower

/-- The remaining positive-frequency quantitative source obligation for one fixed Xi fiber. -/
def FixedFiberPrimeGammaPositiveHighPoissonMargin (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) : Prop :=
  ∀ z : ℂ, 4 < z.re → 0 < z.im → z.im < 1 / 2 →
    riemannZeta (1 / 2 + z * Complex.I) ≠ 0 →
      ((xiZeroCopyFiber ρ).card : ℝ) * z.im /
          Complex.normSq (xiSpectralPointSupport ρ - z) ≤
        -(continuedPrimeArchSourceRelativeTrace z).im

/-- Ordinary conjugation preserves the multiplicity-weighted Poisson floor after applying the
source reflection `z ↦ -conj z`. -/
theorem fixedFiberPoissonFloor_zeroConj_negConj
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) (z : ℂ) :
    ((xiZeroCopyFiber (xiZeroConjEquiv ρ)).card : ℝ) *
          (-(starRingEnd ℂ) z).im /
        Complex.normSq
          (xiSpectralPointSupport (xiZeroConjEquiv ρ) -
            (-(starRingEnd ℂ) z)) =
      ((xiZeroCopyFiber ρ).card : ℝ) * z.im /
        Complex.normSq (xiSpectralPointSupport ρ - z) := by
  have hcard :
      (xiZeroCopyFiber (xiZeroConjEquiv ρ)).card =
        (xiZeroCopyFiber ρ).card := by
    rw [card_xiZeroCopyFiber, card_xiZeroCopyFiber]
    change Int.toNat ((MeromorphicOn.divisor xi Set.univ)
      ((starRingEnd ℂ) (ρ : ℂ))) =
        Int.toNat ((MeromorphicOn.divisor xi Set.univ) (ρ : ℂ))
    rw [xi_divisor_conj]
  have hden :
      Complex.normSq
          (-(starRingEnd ℂ) (xiSpectralPointSupport ρ) -
            (-(starRingEnd ℂ) z)) =
        Complex.normSq (xiSpectralPointSupport ρ - z) := by
    rw [show
      -(starRingEnd ℂ) (xiSpectralPointSupport ρ) -
          (-(starRingEnd ℂ) z) =
        -(starRingEnd ℂ) (xiSpectralPointSupport ρ - z) by
      rw [map_sub]
      ring]
    rw [Complex.normSq_neg, Complex.normSq_conj]
  rw [hcard, xiSpectralPointSupport_zeroConj]
  unfold xiCenteredNegConj
  rw [hden]
  simp

/-- Two positive-frequency channels recover the global Poisson margin: the original critical
fiber pays the positive tail and its Schwarz conjugate pays the reflected negative tail. -/
theorem fixedFiberPrimeGammaPoissonMargin_of_positiveHigh_self_and_zeroConj
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) (hρ : (ρ : ℂ).re = 1 / 2)
    (hpositive : FixedFiberPrimeGammaPositiveHighPoissonMargin ρ)
    (hpositiveConj :
      FixedFiberPrimeGammaPositiveHighPoissonMargin (xiZeroConjEquiv ρ)) :
    FixedFiberPrimeGammaPoissonMargin ρ := by
  intro z hzIm hzHalf hzeta
  by_cases hzCentral : |z.re| ≤ 4
  · exact fixedCriticalFiber_primeGammaPoissonMargin_four
      ρ hρ z hzIm hzHalf hzCentral
  by_cases hzPositive : 4 < z.re
  · exact hpositive z hzPositive hzIm hzHalf hzeta
  · have hzNegative : z.re < -4 := by
      apply lt_of_not_ge
      intro hminus
      apply hzCentral
      rw [abs_le]
      exact ⟨hminus, le_of_not_gt hzPositive⟩
    let w : ℂ := -(starRingEnd ℂ) z
    have hwRe : 4 < w.re := by
      dsimp only [w]
      simp only [Complex.neg_re, Complex.conj_re]
      linarith
    have hwIm : 0 < w.im := by
      dsimp only [w]
      simp only [Complex.neg_im, Complex.conj_im, neg_neg]
      exact hzIm
    have hwHalf : w.im < 1 / 2 := by
      dsimp only [w]
      simp only [Complex.neg_im, Complex.conj_im, neg_neg]
      exact hzHalf
    have hreflect :=
      continuedPrimeArchSourceRelativeTrace_neg_conj_im z hzIm hzHalf hzeta
    have hwMargin :=
      hpositiveConj w hwRe hwIm hwHalf (by simpa only [w] using hreflect.1)
    rw [show w = -(starRingEnd ℂ) z by rfl,
      fixedFiberPoissonFloor_zeroConj_negConj ρ z, hreflect.2] at hwMargin
    exact hwMargin

/-- A positive-frequency Poisson margin implies the ordinary positive-frequency source sign: the
deleted critical atom has nonnegative upper-half-plane Poisson mass. -/
theorem continuedPrimeArchPositiveHighFrequencyUpperAntiHerglotz_of_fixedFiberMargin
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport)
    (hmargin : FixedFiberPrimeGammaPositiveHighPoissonMargin ρ) :
    ContinuedPrimeArchPositiveHighFrequencyUpperAntiHerglotz := by
  intro z hzIm hzHalf hzRe hzeta
  have hz := hmargin z hzRe hzIm hzHalf hzeta

/-!
# Positive representatives of every zero-mass integer-null direction

The positive and negative parts of an integer-null signed mixture have the same
defect. Applying the same positive repair preserves their difference. Thus the
entire native zero-mass null space is generated by differences of nonnegative
integer-null mixtures with equal mass, preserving every linear observation.
-/

noncomputable section
namespace RHTower.WeilWorkPBAP

open WeilOneSided

/-- The two lattice parts of an integer-null mixture require the same correction. -/
theorem paperNullMassSpace_parts_defect_eq (d : paperNullMassSpace) :
    defect d.1⁺ = defect d.1⁻ := by
  apply sub_eq_zero.mp
  rw [← map_sub, posPart_sub_negPart]
  exact d.property.1

/-- Positive part, repaired to satisfy every integer constraint. -/
def paperNullPositivePart (d : paperNullMassSpace) : WeilTestFn →₀ ℝ :=
  nullRepair d.1⁺

/-- Negative part, repaired by exactly the same positive correction. -/
def paperNullNegativePart (d : paperNullMassSpace) : WeilTestFn →₀ ℝ :=
  nullRepair d.1⁻

theorem paperNullPositivePart_nonneg (d : paperNullMassSpace) (f : WeilTestFn) :
    0 ≤ paperNullPositivePart d f :=
  nullRepair_nonneg (posPart_nonneg d.1) f

theorem paperNullNegativePart_nonneg (d : paperNullMassSpace) (f : WeilTestFn) :
    0 ≤ paperNullNegativePart d f :=
  nullRepair_nonneg (negPart_nonneg d.1) f

@[simp] theorem defect_paperNullPositivePart (d : paperNullMassSpace) :
    defect (paperNullPositivePart d) = 0 := defect_nullRepair _

@[simp] theorem defect_paperNullNegativePart (d : paperNullMassSpace) :
    defect (paperNullNegativePart d) = 0 := defect_nullRepair _

/-- Positive repair retains the original signed mixture exactly. -/
theorem paperNullPositivePart_sub_negativePart (d : paperNullMassSpace) :
    paperNullPositivePart d - paperNullNegativePart d = d.1 := by
  simp only [paperNullPositivePart, paperNullNegativePart, nullRepair,
    paperNullMassSpace_parts_defect_eq d, add_sub_add_right_eq_sub, posPart_sub_negPart]

/-- Zero signed mass becomes equality of the two positive masses. -/
theorem paperNullPositivePart_mass_eq (d : paperNullMassSpace) :
    mixtureSample (paperNullPositivePart d) 0 = mixtureSample (paperNullNegativePart d) 0 := by
  apply sub_eq_zero.mp
  rw [← mixtureSample_sub, paperNullPositivePart_sub_negativePart]
  exact d.property.2

/-- Every complex autocorrelation sample survives the common repair. -/
theorem mixtureSample_paperNullParts_sub (d : paperNullMassSpace) (y : ℝ) :
    mixtureSample (paperNullPositivePart d) y - mixtureSample (paperNullNegativePart d) y =
      mixtureSample d.1 y := by
  rw [← mixtureSample_sub, paperNullPositivePart_sub_negativePart]

/-- The full pole-plus-archimedean energy difference also survives exactly. -/
theorem energy_paperNullParts_sub (d : paperNullMassSpace) :
    energy (paperNullPositivePart d) - energy (paperNullNegativePart d) = energy d.1 := by
  rw [← map_sub, paperNullPositivePart_sub_negativePart]

/-- Exact positive-pair description of the entire native zero-mass integer-null space. -/
theorem mem_paperNullMassSpace_iff_positive_difference (d : WeilTestFn →₀ ℝ) :
    d ∈ paperNullMassSpace ↔ ∃ a b : WeilTestFn →₀ ℝ,
      (∀ f, 0 ≤ a f) ∧ (∀ f, 0 ≤ b f) ∧ defect a = 0 ∧ defect b = 0 ∧
      mixtureSample a 0 = mixtureSample b 0 ∧ a - b = d := by
  constructor
  · intro hd
    let v : paperNullMassSpace := ⟨d, hd⟩
    exact ⟨paperNullPositivePart v, paperNullNegativePart v,
      paperNullPositivePart_nonneg v, paperNullNegativePart_nonneg v,
      defect_paperNullPositivePart v, defect_paperNullNegativePart v,
      paperNullPositivePart_mass_eq v, paperNullPositivePart_sub_negativePart v⟩
  · rintro ⟨a, b, _, _, ha, hb, hm, rfl⟩
    rw [mem_paperNullMassSpace]
    constructor
    · rw [map_sub, ha, hb, sub_self]
    · rw [mixtureSample_sub, hm, sub_self]

end RHTower.WeilWorkPBAP

/-!
# A Cauchy partition preserving total mass exactly

Normalizing the paper's Cauchy probes by their positive lattice sum produces
a countable partition of one. Its discrete density measurements preserve
positive mass exactly and contract L1 error, uniformly in the width.
-/

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable section
namespace RHTower.WeilSpectral

/-- Total Cauchy weight at each real height. -/
def paperCauchyLatticeWeight (k : ℕ) (y : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' n : ℤ, paperCauchyKernel k ((n : ℝ) - y)

theorem paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos (k : ℕ) (y : ℝ) :
    0 < paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y :=
  lt_of_lt_of_le (by unfold paperCauchyKernel; positivity)
    (paperCauchyKernel_half_le_lattice k y)

theorem measurable_paperCauchyLatticeWeight (k : ℕ) : Measurable (paperCauchyLatticeWeight k) :=
  Measurable.tsum fun _n : ℤ => ((continuous_paperCauchyKernel k).comp
    (continuous_const.sub continuous_id)).measurable

/-- A probability distribution on integer sites at each real height. -/
def paperCauchyPartition (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (y : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  paperCauchyKernel k ((n : ℝ) - y) / paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y

theorem paperCauchyPartition_nonneg (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (y : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ paperCauchyPartition k n y :=
  div_nonneg (paperCauchyKernel_nonneg _ _) (paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k y).le

theorem paperCauchyPartition_le_one (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (y : ℝ) :
    paperCauchyPartition k n y ≤ 1 := by
  apply (div_le_one (paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k y)).mpr
  exact (summable_paperCauchyKernel_lattice k y).le_tsum n
    (fun _ _ => paperCauchyKernel_nonneg _ _)

theorem summable_paperCauchyPartition (k : ℕ) (y : ℝ) :
    Summable (fun n : ℤ => paperCauchyPartition k n y) :=
  (summable_paperCauchyKernel_lattice k y).div_const _

theorem tsum_paperCauchyPartition (k : ℕ) (y : ℝ) :
    (∑' n : ℤ, paperCauchyPartition k n y) = 1 := by
  simp only [paperCauchyPartition, tsum_div_const]
  exact div_self (paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k y).ne'

private theorem integrable_div_lattice {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f) (k : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun y => f y / paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y) := by
  have hi : Integrable (fun y => (paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y)⁻¹ * f y) := by
    apply hf.bdd_mul (c := (paperCauchyKernel k (1 / 2))⁻¹)
      (measurable_paperCauchyLatticeWeight k).inv.aestronglyMeasurable
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun y => by
      change ‖(paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y)⁻¹‖ ≤ (paperCauchyKernel k (1 / 2))⁻¹
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr (paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k y).le)]
      simpa only [one_div, paperCauchyLatticeWeight] using one_div_le_one_div_of_le
        (by unfold paperCauchyKernel; positivity : 0 < paperCauchyKernel k (1 / 2))
        (paperCauchyKernel_half_le_lattice k y)
  simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm] using hi

/-- Cauchy measurements normalized to preserve density mass. -/
def paperCauchyPartitionSample (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  paperCauchyDensitySample (fun y => f y / paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y) k n

theorem paperCauchyPartitionSample_eq_integral (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ) :
    paperCauchyPartitionSample f k n = ∫ y, paperCauchyPartition k n y * f y := by
  unfold paperCauchyPartitionSample paperCauchyDensitySample paperCauchyPartition
  apply integral_congr_ae
  exact Eventually.of_forall fun _ => by ring

theorem paperCauchyPartitionSample_nonneg {f : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hf0 : ∀ y, 0 ≤ f y) (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : 0 ≤ paperCauchyPartitionSample f k n :=
  paperCauchyDensitySample_nonneg
    (fun y => div_nonneg (hf0 y) (paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k y).le) k n

theorem summable_paperCauchyPartitionSample {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f)
    (hf0 : ∀ y, 0 ≤ f y) (k : ℕ) : Summable (paperCauchyPartitionSample f k) :=
  paperCauchyDensitySample_summable_nonneg (integrable_div_lattice hf k)
    (fun y => div_nonneg (hf0 y) (paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k y).le) k

/-- The infinite sample sum is exactly the positive density's total mass. -/
theorem tsum_paperCauchyPartitionSample {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f)
    (hf0 : ∀ y, 0 ≤ f y) (k : ℕ) :
    (∑' n : ℤ, paperCauchyPartitionSample f k n) = ∫ y, f y := by
  unfold paperCauchyPartitionSample
  rw [tsum_paperCauchyDensitySample_eq (integrable_div_lattice hf k)
    (fun y => div_nonneg (hf0 y) (paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k y).le)]
  apply integral_congr_ae
  exact Eventually.of_forall fun y => by
    change paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y * (f y / paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y) = f y
    field_simp [(paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k y).ne']

theorem abs_paperCauchyPartitionSample_le (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ) :
    |paperCauchyPartitionSample f k n| ≤ paperCauchyPartitionSample (fun y => |f y|) k n := by
  have h := abs_paperCauchyDensitySample_le
    (f := fun y => f y / paperCauchyLatticeWeight k y) k n
  simpa only [paperCauchyPartitionSample, abs_div,
    abs_of_pos (paperCauchyLatticeWeight_pos k _)] using h

/-!
# Rational correlation remains free on positive integer-null fibres

The paper's prime-subset masks give positive smooth mixtures with equal mass and
zero integer defect. Their difference at `log 2 - log 3` can be any complex
number. Thus integer defects and total mass do not determine rational samples.
The constructive survivor is an exact family of positive null pairs, retaining
the full coprime energy identity from `WeilPaperPacketCoprimeFibre`.
-/

open Complex
noncomputable section
namespace RHTower.WeilWorkPBAP

open WeilOneSided

private def twoThreeRatio : PaperPacketCoprimePair 3 :=
  ⟨(⟨2, by decide⟩, ⟨3, by decide⟩), by decide⟩

private def unitRatio : PaperPacketCoprimePair 3 :=
  ⟨(⟨1, by decide⟩, ⟨1, by decide⟩), by decide⟩

/-- Coefficients producing a prescribed complex difference at the reduced ratio `2/3`. -/
def paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs (z : ℂ) (m : PacketIndex 3) : ℂ :=
  if (m : ℕ) = 2 then z / (packetMass 3 4 : ℂ) else 1

/-- The actual repaired mixtures have an arbitrary prescribed complex sample difference. -/
theorem paperPacket_prime_null_two_three_sample (z : ℂ) :
    mixtureSample (paperPacketEvenPrimeNullMixture 3 (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z))
        (Real.log 2 - Real.log 3) -
      mixtureSample (paperPacketOddPrimeNullMixture 3 (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z))
        (Real.log 2 - Real.log 3) = z := by
  have hm : (packetMass 3 4 : ℂ) ≠ 0 :=
    Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr (packetMass_pos 3 4).ne'
  calc
    _ = (packetMass 3 4 : ℂ) * (z / (packetMass 3 4 : ℂ)) := by
      simpa [twoThreeRatio, paperPacketNonunitCoeff, paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs] using
        paperPacket_prime_null_primitive_sample 0 (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z) twoThreeRatio
    _ = z := by field_simp [hm]

/-- The same construction preserves mass as well as every integer constraint. -/
theorem paperPacket_prime_null_two_three_mass (z : ℂ) :
    mixtureSample (paperPacketEvenPrimeNullMixture 3 (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z)) 0 =
      mixtureSample (paperPacketOddPrimeNullMixture 3 (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z)) 0 := by
  apply sub_eq_zero.mp
  simpa [unitRatio, paperPacketNonunitCoeff] using
    paperPacket_prime_null_primitive_sample 2 (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z) unitRatio

/-- Positive integer-null mixtures with equal mass realize every complex sample difference. -/
theorem exists_positive_null_equal_mass_pair_rational_difference (z : ℂ) :
    ∃ a b : WeilTestFn →₀ ℝ,
      (∀ f, 0 ≤ a f) ∧ (∀ f, 0 ≤ b f) ∧
      defect a = 0 ∧ defect b = 0 ∧
      mixtureSample a 0 = mixtureSample b 0 ∧
      mixtureSample a (Real.log 2 - Real.log 3) -
        mixtureSample b (Real.log 2 - Real.log 3) = z ∧
      energy a - energy b =
        packetArchPairing 4 (paperPacketCoprimeCovariance (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z)) :=
  ⟨paperPacketEvenPrimeNullMixture 3 (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z),
    paperPacketOddPrimeNullMixture 3 (paperPacketTwoThreeCoeffs z),
    paperPacketEvenPrimeNullMixture_nonneg 3 _, paperPacketOddPrimeNullMixture_nonneg 3 _,
    defect_paperPacketEvenPrimeNullMixture 3 _, defect_paperPacketOddPrimeNullMixture 3 _,
    paperPacket_prime_null_two_three_mass z, paperPacket_prime_null_two_three_sample z,
    energy_paperPacket_prime_null_parity 3 _⟩

/-- No rule using integer defects and total mass recovers this rational sample,
even on the cone of nonnegative finite mixtures. -/
theorem no_rational_sample_factor_through_defect_and_mass :
    ¬ ∃ F : (LogIndex →₀ ℝ) → ℂ → ℂ,
      ∀ c : WeilTestFn →₀ ℝ, (∀ f, 0 ≤ c f) →
        mixtureSample c (Real.log 2 - Real.log 3) = F (defect c) (mixtureSample c 0) := by
  rintro ⟨F, hF⟩
  obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hb, ha0, hb0, hm, hs, _⟩ :=
    exists_positive_null_equal_mass_pair_rational_difference 1
  rw [hF a ha, hF b hb, ha0, hb0, hm, sub_self] at hs
  exact zero_ne_one hs

end RHTower.WeilWorkPBAP

/-!
# Finite positive connection of prime-entry third jets

Every prime-entry third jet found in the preceding module is a positive arithmetic scale times one
universal cubic Loewner matrix.  This file aggregates arbitrary finite event packets and arbitrary
atom-dependent scalar dressings.

Nonnegative dressing preserves the universal centered square law.  If one positively dressed event
is a genuine prime power, the arithmetic rate and every nonzero first-clock-moment quadratic are
strictly positive.  The literal visible cutoff therefore defines an unconditional positive
semidefinite third-jet connection on the zero-sum coefficient sector at every aperture.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace RHTower

open Matrix

noncomputable section

/-- Universal cubic Loewner direction shared by every prime-entry third jet. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryUniversalThirdJet (N : ℕ) :
    Matrix (Fin (2 * N + 1)) (Fin (2 * N + 1)) ℝ :=
  fun i j => 2 * Real.pi ^ 2 *
    (ccmPublishedCenteredClock N i ^ 2 +
      ccmPublishedCenteredClock N i * ccmPublishedCenteredClock N j +
      ccmPublishedCenteredClock N j ^ 2) - 3

/-- Each arithmetic third jet is its positive scalar scale times the universal Loewner direction. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryCenteredMatrixJet3_eq_scale_smul
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 < k) (N : ℕ) :
    ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryCenteredMatrixJet3 k N =
      ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale k •
        ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryUniversalThirdJet N := by
  ext i j
  rw [ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryCenteredMatrixJet3_apply hk]
  rfl

/-- Total arithmetic third-jet rate after arbitrary atomwise dressing. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJetRate
    (dressing : ℕ → ℝ) (S : Finset ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ k ∈ S, dressing k * ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale k

/-- Finite matrix-valued third-jet connection after arbitrary atomwise dressing. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJet
    (dressing : ℕ → ℝ) (S : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ) :
    Matrix (Fin (2 * N + 1)) (Fin (2 * N + 1)) ℝ :=
  ∑ k ∈ S, dressing k • ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryCenteredMatrixJet3 k N

/-- **Finite third-jet connection factorization.** Every dressed packet retains one universal cubic
Loewner direction. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJet_eq_rate_smul
    (dressing : ℕ → ℝ) {S : Finset ℕ} (hS : ∀ k ∈ S, 1 < k) (N : ℕ) :
    ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJet dressing S N =
      ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJetRate dressing S •
        ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryUniversalThirdJet N := by
  rw [ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJet,
    ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJetRate]
  calc
    (∑ k ∈ S, dressing k • ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryCenteredMatrixJet3 k N) =
        ∑ k ∈ S, (dressing k * ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale k) •
          ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryUniversalThirdJet N := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro k hk
      rw [ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryCenteredMatrixJet3_eq_scale_smul (hS k hk),
        smul_smul]
    _ = _ := by rw [Finset.sum_smul]

/-- Every index above one has nonnegative third-jet scale. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale_nonneg
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 < k) :
    0 ≤ ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale k := by
  rw [ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale]
  have hw : 0 ≤ criticalMellinAtomWeight k := by
    rw [criticalMellinAtomWeight]
    exact mul_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg k) _)
      ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_nonneg
  have hlog : 0 < Real.log k := Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast hk)
  exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by norm_num) hw) (pow_nonneg hlog.le 3)

/-- Nonnegative dressing with one active prime power gives strictly positive total rate. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJetRate_pos
    {dressing : ℕ → ℝ} {S : Finset ℕ}
    (hS : ∀ k ∈ S, 1 < k) (hdressing : ∀ k ∈ S, 0 ≤ dressing k)
    (hactive : ∃ k ∈ S, IsPrimePow k ∧ 0 < dressing k) :
    0 < ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJetRate dressing S := by
  rw [ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryDressedThirdJetRate]
  have hlt : (∑ _k ∈ S, (0 : ℝ)) <
      ∑ k ∈ S, dressing k * ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale k := by
    apply Finset.sum_lt_sum
    · intro k hk
      exact mul_nonneg (hdressing k hk)
        (ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale_nonneg (hS k hk))
    · obtain ⟨k, hk, hkpow, hdresspos⟩ := hactive
      exact ⟨k, hk, mul_pos hdresspos
        (ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryThirdJetScale_pos hkpow)⟩
  simpa using hlt

/-- Exact outer-product decomposition of the universal cubic Loewner direction. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryUniversalThirdJet_eq_outerProducts
    (N : ℕ) :
    ccmGuinandWeilPrimeEntryUniversalThirdJet N =
      (2 * Real.pi ^ 2) •
          Matrix.vecMulVec
            (fun i : Fin (2 * N + 1) => ccmPublishedCenteredClock N i ^ 2)
            ccmConstantBoundary +
        (2 * Real.pi ^ 2) •
          Matrix.vecMulVec (ccmPublishedCenteredClock N)
